speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues; to start our investigation, how old are you and exactly when did this swelling first begin?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (specifically Oligoarticular JIA, potentially associated with HLA-B27 or genetic predisposition given the family history). The patient is an 18-month-old with unilateral knee swelling and no trauma, which is highly characteristic. I recommend checking inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) and ordering an Antinuclear Antibody (ANA) test to assess risk for uveitis. Additionally, an Ultrasound of the right knee would help confirm synovitis.
